judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports hit all five expectations with equivalent substance and citations; Report 1 is somewhat more exhaustive (e.g. flags the failover runbook discrepancy and pre-send hygiene issues) but the two are comparable in quality on the graded expectations.

report_1.evidence: failures began 14:03 and the FIRST ALERT fired at 14:50 — a 47-minute detection gap

report_2.evidence: checkout failures began at 14:03 and the first alert did not fire until 14:50 — a 47-minute detection gap

report_1.evidence: "1,284 transactions failed and required manual reprocessing; 37 were unrecoverable and refunded."

report_2.evidence: records that 1,284 transactions failed and required manual reprocessing, and 37 were unrecoverable and refunded

report_1.evidence: larkpay-comms/docs/sla-commitments.md sets a contractual *monthly* SLA of 99.9% and says any month below it "is a breach and owes service credits." April 2026 was 99.77% (larkpay-comms/metrics/uptime-2026.csv line 6)

report_2.evidence: larkpay-comms/docs/sla-commitments.md sets a contractual monthly uptime SLA of 99.9% and states any month below it "is a breach and owes service credits"... larkpay-comms/metrics/uptime-2026.csv shows April 2026 at 99.77% — below the SLA.

report_1.evidence: This violates larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md rule 1 ("Never assign blame to an individual")

report_2.evidence: Individual blame must be removed (rule 1: "Never assign blame to an individual"). The draft's root-cause sentence — "The outage was caused by the on-call engineer deploying an untested config change" — pins the outage on a specific person.

report_1.evidence: Style guide rule 3 (larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md) requires leading with impact and remediation; the draft instead opens with a reputation defense (lines 3–4), buries a vague impact statement mid-document (line 6), and leaves remediation to a single closing line (line 21).

report_2.evidence: The draft must be restructured to lead with customer impact and remediation (rule 3). It currently opens with reputation defense (the uptime claim and "commitment to reliability") and devotes a paragraph to praising the engineering culture, while impact is minimized and remediation is a single closing line.
